---
title: "Troubleshooting"
---

Start with `juphyter doctor`. It names the failing part, and for a Python on
the wrong `PATH` it prints the `export` line that fixes it.

## A kernel stopped working

The kernel records absolute paths to a PHP binary, a Python interpreter, and
juphyter itself. Upgrading or removing any of them breaks the kernel, and
`juphyter doctor` marks it `fail`.

- Run `juphyter install` again with the same `--name` to record the current
  paths.
- A kernel installed into a project breaks when the project's `vendor`
  directory is deleted. Run `composer install` in the project, or uninstall
  the kernel.

### Homebrew PHP and juphyter 0.1.0

juphyter 0.1.0 recorded Homebrew's versioned path, such as
`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/php/8.5.10/bin/php`, which `brew upgrade` removes.
juphyter 0.1.1 and later record the path on `PATH`, such as
`/opt/homebrew/bin/php`. Upgrade juphyter and run `juphyter install` again,
or pass the stable path to 0.1.0:

```bash
juphyter install --php /opt/homebrew/bin/php
```

## No Python can host the kernel

`juphyter install` looks for an interpreter in this order: the one named by
`--python`, then the one that owns the `jupyter` command on `PATH`. When that
interpreter has no ipykernel 7, it builds a virtual environment with
JupyterLab instead of installing into it.

- System and Homebrew Python builds are externally managed, and `pip install`
  into them refuses. The virtual environment avoids that.
- An environment that already exists at the `--create-venv` path is reused,
  and its packages are installed again, so a second run finishes an
  interrupted one.
- A directory at that path that holds something other than an environment is
  refused.
- With `--python`, the command builds nothing. When the named interpreter has
  no ipykernel, it prints the `pip install` command for that interpreter and
  writes no kernel.

## The stop button does nothing

The PHP binary that runs the cells lacks `pcntl`, or lists its functions in
`disable_functions`. `juphyter doctor` reports it as a warning. Enable `pcntl`
for that binary, or run `juphyter install --php` with a binary that has it.
[Limitations](limitations.qmd#interrupting-needs-pcntl) covers what an
interrupt can and cannot stop.

## Quarto

### Quarto cannot find the kernel

```
ERROR: Jupyter kernel 'php' not found. Known kernels: python3
```

Quarto's interpreter has no Jupyter in it, so it can list no kernels.
`juphyter doctor` reports this as `Quarto: not ready.` and prints the fix.
[Python interpreters and editors](python.qmd) covers how to point Quarto at
an interpreter that has Jupyter.

### `KeyError: 'path'` with a `kernelspec` block

Quarto accepts the fuller front matter that Jupyter writes into a notebook,
but for juphyter it also needs `path`, the directory that holds `kernel.json`:

```yaml
---
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    name: php85
    language: php
    display_name: "PHP 8.5"
    path: /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php85
---
```

Quarto reads `path` to look for a setup cell beside the kernelspec, which it
does for any language it has no built-in support for. `jupyter: php85` fills
it in, so name the kernel instead of describing it.

### `Unknown message type: 'comm_open'`

Every render prints this once. It comes from ipykernel, because the kernel
installs no comm manager, and it has no effect on the rendered document. The
same absence is why ipywidgets are unsupported.

### A new PHP session on every render

Quarto keeps a kernel alive between renders only for languages it can write a
setup or cleanup cell for. It has none for PHP, and `juphyter install` writes
none, so each render starts a new PHP session even with
`--execute-daemon`. To keep that behavior if a later Quarto release changes
it, set:

```yaml
execute:
  daemon: false
```

A document that declares a class or a function depends on it, because PHP
cannot redeclare either in a kept-alive session.

### Rendering frozen documents

Quarto looks up a document's kernel by name before it reads frozen output, so
a kernel with that name has to be registered on the rendering machine even
when no cell runs. [Contributing](development.qmd#documentation) shows how
this repository renders its own site that way.
